claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is prone to cracking.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a significant caloric response under operational applied fields.
The as-cast or conventionally processed alloy has a relatively homogeneous grain structure.
The relatively homogeneous grain structure is prone to crack initiation and propagation.
Deformation followed by controlled annealing can generate a heterogeneous grain structure in this alloy.
The proposed thermo-mechanical processing can increase the density of twin boundaries in this alloy.
Twin boundaries and heterogeneous grain sizes will impede and deflect crack propagation.
Twin boundaries and heterogeneous grain sizes will promote local strain accommodation.
Impeded crack propagation and local strain accommodation will increase the alloy's toughness and mechanical integrity.
The thermo-mechanical treatment will not significantly alter the alloy composition.
The thermo-mechanical treatment will preserve the phase transition responsible for the caloric effect.
Preserving the phase transition will maintain caloric performance.
The processed alloy will have greater crack resistance than the unchanged alloy.
The processed alloy will have greater load-bearing capacity and fracture toughness than the unchanged alloy.
The processed alloy will retain a caloric-response magnitude similar to that of the unchanged alloy under magnetic fields.
The processed alloy will retain a caloric-response magnitude similar to that of the unchanged alloy under pressure fields.
The predicted benefits apply near the alloy's phase-transition temperature under typical magnetic-field and pressure ranges.
Excessive deformation or annealing may substantially alter the phase-transition behavior and lies outside the predicted beneficial processing window.
